scope: All 1502 Vitest-expanded baseline test cases across 143 files. Declaration sources/assertions are from baseline HEAD, not later refactor additions.
method: Every baseline source test body, relevant setup/helper and input table was manually read and evaluated for redundancy. All 1502 expanded cases map to the 941 reviewed declarations. Each case retains its actual input identity; each declaration retains parameter and assertion evidence plus a manual rationale. Similar callbacks were compared across setup, operation, input and observed state. Only two equivalent coverage replacements were established and removed. This is not a mutation-testing proof or a claim that every retained assertion is indispensable.

cases.expandedTitle: cancels synchronously, drains admitted work, and rejects its late result

cases.expandedTitle: rejects stale operations and all work after terminal release
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: rejects stale operations and all work after terminal release. Terminal release must forbid reacquisition and new authoritative work and expose released state; the cancellation tests concern work admitted before shutdown.

cases.expandedTitle: cancels an acquisition that settles after shutdown begins
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: cancels an acquisition that settles after shutdown begins. Acquire and shutdown race before acquisition settles must reject it, followed by a fresh authority successfully starting generation one. Pending-operation draining does not cover pending acquisition.

cases.expandedTitle: corrupt-header download recovers a real backup with local conflict choice and preserves both sources
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: corrupt-header download recovers a real backup with local conflict choice and preserves both sources. cases.name: corrupt-header download recovers a real backup with cloud conflict choice and preserves both sources
cases.expandedTitle: corrupt-header download recovers a real backup with cloud conflict choice and preserves both sources

cases.name: future-version backup stops downgrade recovery and leaves all files untouched
cases.expandedTitle: future-version backup stops downgrade recovery and leaves all files untouched
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: future-version backup stops downgrade recovery and leaves all files untouched. Future first backup ahead of a valid older backup must stop recovery and retain remote bytes with no local save, preventing a silent downgrade that corrupt-backup skipping would miss.

cases.name: healthy checkpoints transferred in both directions load as Cloud saves, not backup recovery
cases.expandedTitle: healthy checkpoints transferred in both directions load as Cloud saves, not backup recovery

cases.name: independent local progress after a successful sync still requires a preserved conflict choice
cases.expandedTitle: independent local progress after a successful sync still requires a preserved conflict choice
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: independent local progress after a successful sync still requires a preserved conflict choice. cases.expandedTitle: offline progress is copied into the account, survives restart and preserves both original profiles

cases.expandedTitle: keeping the account dismisses only this offline snapshot; deferring asks again
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: keeping the account dismisses only this offline snapshot; deferring asks again. Exercises later versus account choices over repeated calls and a changed offline fingerprint, proving deferral repeats while explicit dismissal applies only to one snapshot.

cases.expandedTitle: an interrupted selection leaves originals intact and can retry without trusting a partial copy

cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: linked offline files and missing selected roots fail closed. Deleted selected root and symlinked source are distinct fail-closed inputs; verifies unsafe source fails before prompt. Normal copy tests cannot replace path integrity coverage.

cases.expandedTitle: offline preferences alone do not offer an empty profile over an account save
cases.rationale: Expanded scenario: offline preferences alone do not offer an empty profile over an account save. A policy/preferences file without gameplay save must not trigger offering an empty offline profile; ordinary empty-directory startup does not exercise misleading non-save artifacts.

cases.name: an uncommitted partial copy is ignored when retrying from the durable old selection

declarations.title: holds at Overflow without rewards or a reset (auto=$automatic, continuous=$continuous)
declarations.expression:
test.each([
    { automatic: false, continuous: false },
    { automatic: true, continuous: false },
    { automatic: false, continuous: true },
    { automatic: true, continuous: true },
  ])
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ consumedMilliseconds: 100, remainingMilliseconds: 0, checkpoints: ['pending'], transition: { accepted: true }, })
expect(held.infinity).toMatchObject({ points: before.gameState.infinity.points, automaticResetEnabled: automatic, botCapTransitionPending: true, botCapRewardsGranted: false, inProgress: false, })
declarations.manualRationale: All combinations of automatic Infinity and fixed/continuous active delivery must stop at Overflow with one pending checkpoint, no reward/reset, persistence across reopen and blocked ordinary/Quantum resets. Distinct engine admission modes must retain this gameplay boundary.

declarations.title: retries an eligibility checkpoint failure without granting anything
declarations.manualRationale: Failure on eligibility checkpoint keeps rewards untouched and retry persists pending status only; later reset failure exercises a different durable stage.

declarations.title: publishes a single full reset only after its save succeeds, and reopens the point balance
assertions: expect(await pending).toMatchObject({ kind: 'transition', transition: { accepted: true, changed: true } })
expect(reset.gameState.avocado).toEqual({ unlocked: true, infinityPoints: 0, influence: 0, strangeMatter: 0, overflowMultiplier: 0, overflowPoints: 1n, })
declarations.manualRationale: Gated voluntary Overflow reset stays invisible until save, resets full progression while preserving presets/secrets/entitlements, rewards exactly once despite stale/repeated commands, and resumes after reopen. Pure reset unit tests omit commit and revision fences.

declarations.title: failed reset persistence preserves the run and retries for exactly one point
declarations.manualRationale: Failed reset commit preserves ready state and pending eligibility across restart, then rewards exactly one point on retry; successful gated commit never exercises durable-write failure.

declarations.title: a premature reset does not write or change progression
declarations.manualRationale: Premature voluntary reset must reject with unchanged state and zero repository commits; repeated request after a completed reset has different durable history.

declarations.title: eligibility survives Stellar spending and reload without another reward
declarations.manualRationale: Once eligibility is earned, reducing bots below cap (Stellar spending) and reopening must retain reset availability without extra reward; cap-held state tests cannot detect recomputing eligibility from current bots.

declarations.title: advances an ordinary tick without cloning complete runtime state
declarations.manualRationale: Clone spy around actual transactional engine proves ordinary tick and immutable snapshots reuse shallow-fork publication without full runtime cloning; generic engine tests do not exercise this concrete definition.

declarations.title: replaces changed branches without mutating a shallow-fork source
assertions: expect(definition.applyCommand(commandCandidate, { kind: 'internal.development-set-dyson-bots', bots: 1_000, })).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Advancing and development-command application against shallow forks must replace branches without mutating original graph; frozen-engine coverage could conceal direct definition mutation behind clone behavior.

declarations.title: sets the development bot count through the current canonical allocation
declarations.manualRationale: Setting absolute bot count with 25% research allocation must recompute 750 workers/250 researchers; signed add-bots test only checks total, not synchronized allocation.

declarations.title: rejects normal Infinity at a checkpointed Overflow boundary
declarations.manualRationale: Checkpointed Overflow with pending flag and MAX_VALUE bots must reject ordinary Infinity without changing points/bots; uncheckpointed case requires a different error and pending state.

declarations.title: allows manual Break Infinity below the configured automatic target
assertions: expect(definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'infinity.request-reset', })).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Manual Break reset just above ordinary threshold must ignore higher automatic target and grant one IP with auto disabled; automatic reset timing tests do not establish manual override.

declarations.title: rejects manual Infinity until the finite bot-cap checkpoint is durable
declarations.manualRationale: Uncheckpointed finite bot-cap manual reset must return persistence-required code and preserve full state; already-pending Overflow rejection takes a different guard.

declarations.title: rejects an invalid development bot count without changing state
declarations.manualRationale: Absolute bot-setting NaN rejects with dedicated BOTS-INVALID error and unchanged state; add-resource validation goes through a different internal command.

declarations.title: unlocks tabs without altering progression and accepts repeated requests unchanged
assertions: expect(definition.applyCommand(state, command)).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
expect(definition.applyCommand(state, command)).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: false })
declarations.manualRationale: Unlock-all-tabs changes only runtime flag and second identical request is accepted unchanged; frontend visibility projection does not test mutator idempotence.

declarations.title: applies a coherent development Reality unlock state
declarations.manualRationale: Development Reality unlock must coherently raise total/spent points and Secrets to 27 together; resource additions do not maintain this synthetic unlock invariant.

declarations.title: applies Unity-parity development grants through one canonical action
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Positive grants route five distinct resource actions and must report changed with increased balances; negative-floor tests traverse decrement paths and cannot establish positive dispatch routing.

declarations.title: runs Unity auto-assignment immediately after granting skill points
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-skill-points', amount: 1n }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Granting one Skill Point must immediately purchase queued assemblyLine and consume point; generic positive grant with no targeted queue cannot detect missing auto-assignment.

declarations.title: keeps a maximum Skill Point developer grant playable with Purity
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-skill-points', amount: DISCRETE_MAXIMUM, }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Maximum Skill Point grant with three Purity skills explicitly verifies finite internal globals, rates, facility modifiers and next evaluation snapshot through the engine helper. Browser integration checks exposed snapshot/save finiteness, not an established one-to-one witness for every internal evaluation field; retain the focused numeric boundary.

declarations.title: reopens an affected maximum Skill Point Purity save
declarations.manualRationale: Already-maxed schema08-derived Purity state is prepared/reopened directly and all three ownership flags plus internal derivation/evaluation finiteness are asserted. Browser integration adds Stored Time before reopen and checks published fields, so it does not exactly replace this immediate pre-replay reopen witness.

declarations.title: retains zero-point development auto-assignment behavior
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-skill-points', amount: 0n }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Zero Skill Point grant still runs existing queue using available point; this deliberately protects zero-trigger behavior distinct from a positive grant.

declarations.title: publishes the exact skill preset application outcome as transient runtime state
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'skill.select-preset', slot: 2, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })

expect(state.lastSkillPresetApplication).toMatchObject({ applicationSequence: 1, slot: 2, trigger: 'manual', retainedSkillIds: expect.any(Array), assignedSkillIds: expect.any(Array), pendingSkillIds: expect.any(Array), blockedByRetainedSkillIds: expect.any(Array), })
expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'skill.select-preset', slot: 2, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Preset application updates transient outcome sequence on repeated same-slot selections; desired-layout persistence does not assert repeated notification sequence.

declarations.title: routes an automatic partial preset result through sequenced presentation events
assertions: expect(definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'skill.apply-tab-preset-automation', tab: 'bots', })).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })

expect(state.presentationEvents).toEqual([ expect.objectContaining({ kind: 'skill-preset-conflict', sequence: 1, presetName: 'Conflict preset', application: expect.objectContaining({ trigger: 'automatic', blockedByRetainedSkillIds: ['shouldersOfTheEnlightened'], }), }), ])

expect.objectContaining({ kind: 'skill-preset-conflict', sequence: 1, presetName: 'Conflict preset', application: expect.objectContaining({ trigger: 'automatic', blockedByRetainedSkillIds: ['shouldersOfTheEnlightened'], }), })
declarations.manualRationale: Automatic tab preset with retained mutual exclusion emits named sequenced partial-conflict event; manual application outcome test has no automated conflict notification.

declarations.title: publishes a sequenced automatic-disaster event with pre-reset facts
assertions: expect(state.presentationEvents).toEqual([ expect.objectContaining({ kind: 'automatic-dream-disaster', sequence: 1, cause: 'Meteor', strangeMatterGranted: 1, resetCount: 1n, firstLifetimeOccurrence: true, preResetEra: 'information', }), ])
expect.objectContaining({ kind: 'automatic-dream-disaster', sequence: 1, cause: 'Meteor', strangeMatterGranted: 1, resetCount: 1n, firstLifetimeOccurrence: true, preResetEra: 'information', })
declarations.manualRationale: Automatic dream disaster captures pre-reset era/reward/count and marks first lifetime occurrence only once across two triggers; disaster simulation tests do not cover application event projection.

declarations.title: restores the development cash action without changing player commands
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-cash', amount: 125 }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Positive cash grant asserts exact prior-plus-125 arithmetic through internal action; shared positive resource loop excludes cash.

declarations.title: applies signed development resource adjustments with canonical floors
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Negative adjustments across resources clamp zero or already-spent discrete floor and must not trigger queued Skill purchase; positive dispatch and invalid amount tests cannot replace decrement semantics.

declarations.title: applies signed Stored Time adjustments without advancing gameplay
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-offline-time', seconds: -1 }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-offline-time', seconds: -1_000 }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Negative Stored Time decrement preserves capacity and double-time bank, clamps at zero and leaves Dyson/statistics unchanged; positive bank credit invokes a different grant policy.

declarations.title: rejects non-finite and out-of-range signed development amounts atomically
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action, }), ).toMatchObject({ accepted: false, code: 'CANONICAL-DEVELOPMENT-ACTION-INVALID', })
declarations.manualRationale: Non-finite continuous and out-of-range signed bigint inputs reject atomically with ACTION-INVALID; test values represent NaN, both infinity signs and both discrete overflow directions across routed fields.

declarations.title: credits debug offline time without advancing active gameplay
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'add-offline-time', seconds: 1_000 }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Positive offline-time grant clamps available bank to capacity, applies double-time interaction and never advances Dyson/statistics; real Stored Time replay is intentionally different.

declarations.title: resets Avotation secret progress through Developer Options
assertions: expect( definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'reset-secret-progress' }, }), ).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Developer secret reset clears both completion and step from completed seven-state; no other development resource action touches this domain.

declarations.title: purchases, disables, and freely re-enables Developer Options
declarations.manualRationale: Purchasing Developer Options debits two currencies once, disabling preserves ownership, and reenabling is free; host entitlement grant cannot establish local purchase history.

declarations.title: charges a representable Strange Matter step for Developer Options at the double cap
assertions: expect(definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'purchase-debug-options' }, })).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Developer purchase at Number.MAX_VALUE Strange Matter must consume one representable floating-point step, preventing free purchases hidden by rounding; ordinary affordability case uses small exact numbers.

declarations.title: applies trusted host entitlements without persisting a paid save claim
assertions: expect(definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.replace-host-entitlements', entitlements: { permanentDoubleIp: true }, })).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
expect(definition.applyCommand(state, { kind: 'internal.development-apply-action', action: { kind: 'enable-host-debug-options' }, })).toEqual({ accepted: true, changed: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Trusted host Double IP and debug enablement must update runtime without setting local paid entitlement flag; in-game purchase deliberately sets that flag.

declarations.title: routes player settings with runtime carriers as one transaction
declarations.manualRationale: Concrete application engine routes normal buy-mode command with its runtime carriers as accepted changed state; command router unit tests bypass this facade-to-router bridge.

declarations.title: keeps Tinker outside a stored-time candidate
declarations.manualRationale: Tinker-running and idle candidates replay identical bots/facilities while retaining transient Tinker and presentation events and debiting bank; worker/serialization tests do not exercise synchronous replay against active Tinker.

declarations.title: settles a final-update bot cap in synchronous Stored Time replay
assertions: expect(state.gameState.infinity).toMatchObject({ points: pointsBefore, botCapTransitionPending: true, botCapRewardsGranted: false, inProgress: false, })
declarations.manualRationale: Final Stored Time update hitting Overflow must settle pending boundary without granting IP/overflow and debit entire 0.1s even when event timer reaches zero; active cap checkpoint tests use a different settlement lane.

declarations.title: forces Buy Max for stored-time automation without changing the configured mode
declarations.manualRationale: Paired active versus Stored Time replay proves forced Max automation only in stored lane for facilities and research while retaining configured buy-1; one-lane automation tests cannot establish mode isolation.

declarations.title: discards the whole stored-time candidate when cancellation follows progress
declarations.manualRationale: Cancellation after at least one replay progress poll discards whole synchronous candidate and preserves source; before-start cancellation cannot detect partial mutation leakage.

declarations.title: previews Quantum Leap non-mutatingly with exact gate and branch
assertions: expect(previewCanonicalQuantumLeap(state, context())).toEqual({ eligible: false, code: 'QUANTUM_LEAP_REQUIRES_42_TOTAL_INFINITY_POINTS', branch: null, artifactSkillPoints: null, definitionGap: null, })
declarations.manualRationale: Quantum preview below 42 IP returns exact gate, then entangled branch at 42 without mutating either input; actual leap certification exercises transactions rather than non-mutating preview.

declarations.title: mobile candidates retain a proven milestone before a later command removes its condition
declarations.manualRationale: Forking with achievement retention captures milestone before later bot reduction without mutating source evidence; achievement evaluation alone does not cover transactional carry-forward across a condition-removing command.

declarations.title: persists known and unvisited navigation routes idempotently
declarations.manualRationale: Route-discovery command stores ordered known/unvisited arrays and repeated identical input is unchanged; navigation visibility toggles write a different preference slice.

declarations.title: updates a persisted navigation shortcut preference idempotently
declarations.manualRationale: Story shortcut toggle changes its saved flag then returns accepted unchanged for same value; discovery idempotence does not establish shortcut command behavior.

declarations.title: updates every known destination without discarding future entries
declarations.manualRationale: Updating known store destination preserves seeded future-destination key, guarding forward-compatible preference merge absent in plain story toggles.

declarations.title: keeps an exhaustive routable example for every union member
assertions: expect(result).toEqual( expect.objectContaining({ accepted: expect.any(Boolean), changed: expect.any(Boolean), code: expect.any(String), state: expect.any(Object), issues: expect.any(Array), runtimeCarriers: expect.any(Object), intents: expect.any(Array), }), )
declarations.manualRationale: Compile-time coverage plus runtime iteration over every command kind checks result envelopes and unchanged rejected identity; focused success cases cannot detect a newly added union route missing from dispatch.

declarations.title: publishes a changed state and refreshed evaluation snapshot atomically
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'dyson-facility:success', })
declarations.manualRationale: Frozen Matrioshka purchase must publish changed state plus exact newly evaluated carrier together, with evaluator called against post-purchase state; pure domain transaction lacks runtime carrier atomicity.

declarations.title: rolls back the whole transaction when runtime evaluation rejects
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: false, changed: false, code: 'runtime-evaluation-rejected', })
declarations.manualRationale: Runtime evaluator rejection after otherwise valid purchase must restore exact original state and carrier identities, distinct from a domain gate rejecting before evaluation.

declarations.title: preserves exact state identity when a delegated domain gate rejects
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: false, changed: false, code: 'dyson-facility:locked', })
declarations.manualRationale: Locked Galactic Brains purchase must preserve exact source identity and domain-specific error code; exhaustive smoke table does not include this facility ID.

declarations.title: routes representative Dream, Reality, Quantum, Avocado, and time actions
assertions: expect(dream).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'dream-foundational:success', })
expect(reality).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'reality-gather:success', })
expect(quantum).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'quantum-upgrade:purchased', })
expect(quantumBulk).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'quantum-upgrade:purchased', state: { quantum: { cashBonusLevels: 10n, pointsSpent: 11n, }, }, })
expect(avocado).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'avocado:fed', })
declarations.manualRationale: Explicit affordable Dream/Reality/Quantum/Avocado scenarios exercise successful delegation and quantity forwarding, including ten Cash levels; exhaustive example table may reject on starting-state gates.

declarations.title: synchronizes bot allocation immediately when selecting a preset
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:preset-selected', state: { dyson: { botDistribution: 0.8, workers: 2, researchers: 8, }, }, runtimeCarriers: { selectedSkillPresetSlot: 2, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Selecting preset two with 80% allocation updates workers/researchers immediately and selected runtime slot; saved layout-only checks do not verify bot reallocation.

declarations.title: adds dependency closure to the active and selected preset queues
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:preset-skill-added', state: { skills: { activeAutoAssignment: expected, }, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Adding Androids to default selected slot expands exact dependency order in both desired and live queues and returns added code; certification uses non-default slot and asserts different cross-slot invariants.

declarations.title: removes queued dependants from the active and selected preset queues
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:preset-skill-removed', state: { skills: { activeAutoAssignment: expected, }, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Removing worker efficiency removes dependent Androids while retaining unrelated Banking and panel lifetime, in live and desired queues; certification removal fixture has no unrelated Banking sentinel.

declarations.title: synchronizes manual assignment only into the selected preset
declarations.manualRationale: Manual skill purchase synchronizes only selected slot two and leaves prior Banking preset identity intact; queue-edit commands bypass purchase-to-preset synchronization.

declarations.title: unassigns from only the selected preset and preserves the other four
declarations.manualRationale: Single-skill refund clears selected slot three/live queue while four equivalent saved layouts retain identity and contents; reset-all uses a separate route.

declarations.title: Reset Skills clears only the selected desired layout
declarations.manualRationale: Reset Skills clears only slot four desired/live layout and retains other preset object identities; refund route cannot cover reset-all synchronization.

declarations.title: previews retained conflicts and applies compatible preset parts only after confirmation
assertions: expect(blocked).toMatchObject({ accepted: false, changed: false, code: 'skill:preset-retained-conflict', })
expect(confirmed).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, runtimeCarriers: { selectedSkillPresetSlot: 2 }, })

expect(confirmed.skillPresetApplication).toEqual({ slot: 2, trigger: 'manual', retainedSkillIds: [ 'shouldersOfGiants', 'shouldersOfPrecursors', ], assignedSkillIds: [], pendingSkillIds: ['shouldersOfTheEnlightened'], blockedByRetainedSkillIds: ['shouldersOfTheEnlightened'], })
expect(stale).toMatchObject({ accepted: false, changed: false, code: 'skill:preset-preview-stale', })
declarations.manualRationale: Retained conflict requires explicit matching confirmation, publishes exact retained/pending report on success and rejects stale confirmation identity; automatic partial application intentionally bypasses manual confirmation.

declarations.title: reselects the stored current preset without copying a divergent live queue
declarations.manualRationale: Reselecting already-current saved empty layout must refund divergent live ownership instead of overwriting desired queue; switching different slots does not cover same-slot rebuild.

declarations.title: imports a validated Unity v1 preset atomically and rejects malformed input
assertions: expect(imported).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:preset-imported-and-loaded', state: { dyson: { botDistribution: 0.8 }, skills: { activeAutoAssignment: [], }, }, })
expect(rejected).toMatchObject({ accepted: false, changed: false, code: 'skill:preset-import-unsupported-version', })
declarations.manualRationale: Valid v1 preset import changes name/color/distribution/queue atomically and unsupported version99 preserves original identity; transfer parser tests bypass command loading and application.

declarations.title: sets a validated preset color without changing its queue
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:preset-color-set', })
declarations.manualRationale: Preset color mutation changes metadata only, preserving desired and active queues; full preset import could pass even if color-only command accidentally reassigned skills.

declarations.title: persists and immediately applies a nonzero tab preset override
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:tab-preset-automation-set-and-applied', state: { dyson: { botDistribution: 0.8 }, skills: { tabPresetAutomation: { research: 2 }, }, }, runtimeCarriers: { selectedSkillPresetSlot: 2, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Setting nonzero research-tab override persists slot and immediately applies its bot distribution and runtime selection; applying existing override is a separate command.

declarations.title: automatically applies compatible preset parts around retained skills
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:tab-preset-applied', runtimeCarriers: { selectedSkillPresetSlot: 2 }, })

expect(result.skillPresetApplication).toEqual({ slot: 2, trigger: 'automatic', retainedSkillIds: [ 'shouldersOfGiants', 'shouldersOfPrecursors', ], assignedSkillIds: ['banking'], pendingSkillIds: ['shouldersOfTheEnlightened'], blockedByRetainedSkillIds: ['shouldersOfTheEnlightened'], })
declarations.manualRationale: Automatic tab application keeps retained conflicting ownership, purchases compatible Banking and reports exact assigned/pending IDs without rewriting desired presets; manual confirmed partial case has no compatible purchased skill.

declarations.title: rebuilds an automatic preset even when it is already selected
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'skill:tab-preset-applied', })
declarations.manualRationale: Already-selected automatic preset still rebuilds owned skills and refunds one point for empty desired layout; same-slot manual selection covers a different command path.

declarations.title: delegates Leap gate and branch choice without command-supplied rewards
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'quantum-leap:entanglement', })
declarations.manualRationale: Quantum leap route must invoke injected authoritative port exactly once with original state and relay branch/result, keeping rewards out of command payload; integrated leap result alone does not assert port delegation.

declarations.title: toggles automatic Infinity before or after Break The Loop without runtime evaluation
assertions: expect(disabled).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'infinity-automatic-reset:set', state: { infinity: { automaticResetEnabled: false, currentCyclePeakIpPerMinute: 0, currentCyclePeakReward: 0n, }, }, })
expect(unchanged).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: false, code: 'infinity-automatic-reset:unchanged', })

expect(enabled).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, state: { infinity: { automaticResetEnabled: true, currentCyclePeakIpPerMinute: 74_208.1448, currentCyclePeakReward: 82n, manualPeakIpPerMinute: 74_208.1448, manualPeakReward: 82n, activeAutomaticThroughputCycleEligible: false, }, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Automatic Infinity toggle clears stale throughput, captures mature manual calibration but preserves established peak on short immature intervals, and skips unnecessary evaluation; simple checkbox routing lacks these history-sensitive effects.

declarations.title: invalidates automatic throughput measurement when target or cadence changes
declarations.manualRationale: Changing Break target or processing cadence invalidates automatic-cycle eligibility and history even while auto state is unchanged; toggle tests exercise different invalidation triggers.

declarations.title: invalidates Infinity calibration and throughput when permanent Double Time is purchased
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'reality-upgrade:purchased', state: { infinity: { currentCyclePeakIpPerMinute: 0, currentCyclePeakReward: 0n, manualPeakIpPerMinute: 0, manualPeakReward: 0n, manualCalibrationObservedActiveSeconds: 0, activeAutomaticThroughputCycleEligible: false, }, timeline: { doubleTime: { unlocked: true }, }, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Purchasing permanent Double Time must clear both manual/current calibration and automatic history without mutating source; ordinary Reality upgrades and cadence change do not clear the same full set.

declarations.title: routes manual Infinity through the event-model reset port
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'infinity-reset:APPLIED', state: { infinity: { points: next.infinity.points } }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Manual Infinity route invokes injected event reset port once with original state and propagates code/result; direct engine manual-reset tests use concrete model rather than verifying this adapter contract.

declarations.title: returns stored-time repair metadata with state as one transaction
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ accepted: true, changed: true, code: 'time-stored-capacity:upgraded', state: { timeline: { storedTimeAvailableSeconds: 0, storedTimeCapacitySeconds: 200, }, }, runtimeCarriers: { storedTimeCheater: false }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Stored capacity upgrade atomically consumes bank, doubles capacity and returns repair carrier while leaving input unchanged; time-domain helper tests omit runtime-carrier projection.

declarations.title: keeps the tab override across a local checkpoint and reopen
declarations.manualRationale: Local unlockAllTabs override survives prepare/reopen while canonical gameplay state stays equal; runtime carrier test does not set this override.

declarations.title: mobile evidence survives save/reopen and does not leak into a different imported save
declarations.manualRationale: Persisted achievement evidence survives shared serialization/reopen but does not contaminate a different imported prepared save; sanitization test covers malformed IDs, not session separation.

declarations.title: malformed optional achievement evidence cannot block a save or submit unknown IDs
declarations.manualRationale: Malformed optional evidence with duplicates, unknown string and non-string item must sanitize to one known ID without blocking opening; valid evidence roundtrip cannot establish this fail-soft filter.

declarations.title: persists state, evaluation and out-of-model fields atomically but not Tinker
declarations.manualRationale: One prepared session atomically retains money/evaluation/cheater/selected slot while clearing transient Tinker and preset feedback; pure mapper tests do not own these runtime carriers.

declarations.title: extracts compatibility and evaluation carriers from every imported save
declarations.manualRationale: Two saves opened through one factory carry different panels-per-second evaluation and compatibility multiplier values; this catches factory-level stale capture absent in a single roundtrip.

declarations.title: refuses to prepare an invalid numeric graph for durable storage
assertions: expect(() => session.prepare(state)).toThrow( /Canonical game state is invalid/, )
declarations.manualRationale: Session.prepare rejects NaN in canonical money before storage, preserving the validation boundary rather than relying on later repository repair.

declarations.title: creates first-run saves from the current host UTC sample
declarations.manualRationale: Production first-run factory samples host clock at invocation and embeds that dateStarted; deterministic artifact and explicit-timestamp factory tests bypass this host-clock composition.

declarations.title: samples import UTC before creating the replacement save
declarations.manualRationale: A sequential clock proves reset request captures import timestamp before invoking first-run factory and approves overwrite, preserving ordering when samples differ rather than merely timestamp validity.

declarations.title: matches the checked-in Unity and generated-catalog provenance
declarations.manualRationale: Verifies retained artifact, decoded binary and all generated catalog hashes against provenance plus canonical newline handling; runtime mapping tests assume these historical bytes rather than proving their identity.

declarations.title: round-trips Unity defaults through the normalized Web mapping
declarations.manualRationale: Hydrate/dehydrate first-run artifact must preserve canonical state and classify every storage-shape delta against allowed manifest counts; generic save roundtrip does not witness legacy-to-canonical representation changes.

declarations.title: applies Web lifecycle, Infinity, and navigation defaults only to first-run saves
assertions: expect(production.bottomNavigationPreferences).toMatchObject({ version: 1, routeDiscovery: { knownRoutes: [], unvisitedRoutes: [], }, visibility: { bots: true, research: true, skills: true, infinity: true, reality: true, simulations: true, quantum: true, store: true, story: false, wiki: true, 'offline-time': false, statistics: false, settings: true, }, })

expect(differences.filter(({ path }) => !path.startsWith('$.dysonVerseSaveData'))).toEqual([ { path: '$.dateStarted', expected: deterministic.dateStarted, actual: hostFirstRunUtc, reason: 'value', }, { path: '$.infinityAutomaticReset', expected: true, actual: false, reason: 'value', }, { path: '$.bottomNavigationPreferences', expected: undefined, actual: production.bottomNavigationPreferences, reason: 'missing', }, ])
expect(() => createUnityFirstRunPreparedSave({ startedAtUtc: 'not-a-date' }), ).toThrow('First-run start timestamp is invalid')
declarations.manualRationale: Production first-run overrides only documented lifecycle, navigation, Infinity and bot-distribution defaults, and rejects bad UTC; protects intentional first-run-only deltas without treating Unity defaults as all gameplay authority.

declarations.title: reconstructs and reloads an empty development repository
declarations.manualRationale: Empty repository resolves authentic first-run artifact, commits, reconstructs and compares both portable graph and canonical hydration; explicit factory-clock tests do not exercise verified persistence.

declarations.title: does not advertise Simulation access from lifetime Influence after Overflow
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(reset.state).simulations).toMatchObject({ routeVisible: false, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 0, fraction: 0 }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Overflow clears Reality prerequisite while retained lifetime manual influence alone must not advertise Simulations; restoring Quantum prerequisite reuses that lifetime unlock. Other tests never reset prerequisite under retained statistics.

declarations.title: teases the first facility before it is visible
declarations.manualRationale: Fresh first-run state has no visible facilities but must show next-facility teaser; route-specific tests do not assert this onboarding affordance.

declarations.title: keeps Skills hidden until a Skill Point has actually been earned
declarations.manualRationale: Ten bots alone cannot reveal Skills; earning one point changes hidden to visible/unlocked. Distinct preconditions prevent accidental shortcut from unrelated bot progression.

declarations.title: reveals locked Infinity when Planets become available
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(planetsAvailable).infinity).toMatchObject({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentBots: initial.dyson.bots, requiredBots: 4.2e19, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Data-center ownership revealing Planets must tease locked Infinity with exact bot requirement, separating visibility from actual unlock.

declarations.title: reveals locked Quantum after the first Infinity
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(afterInfinity).quantum).toEqual({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfinityPoints: 0n, requiredInfinityPoints: 42n, fraction: 0, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: First Infinity flag reveals locked Quantum with 42-point progress target; raw Quantum earned resources or Reality prerequisites cover different progression gates.

declarations.title: reveals Reality after the first Secret with Secrets-only progress
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(infinityPointsWithoutSecrets).reality).toEqual({ routeVisible: false, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentSecrets: 0n, requiredSecrets: 27n, fraction: 0, }, })
expect(selectGameplayVisibility(nearSecretsPath).reality).toMatchObject({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentSecrets: 1n, requiredSecrets: 27n, fraction: 1 / 27, }, })
expect(selectGameplayVisibility(nearSecretsPath).simulations).toEqual({ routeVisible: false, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 0, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 0, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: One Secret reveals Reality but 42 IP without Secrets does not; asserts Secrets-only progress and still-hidden Simulations to prevent conflating two resource paths.

declarations.title: previews Simulations after Reality is visited and unlocks it at 128 manual Influence
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(afterQuantumLeap).simulations).toEqual({ routeVisible: false, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 0, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 0, }, })
expect(selectGameplayVisibility(afterRealityVisit).simulations).toEqual({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 0, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 0, }, })

expect( selectGameplayVisibility(generationInProgress.state).simulations, ).toEqual({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 127, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 127.5 / 128, }, })

expect(selectGameplayVisibility(readyToGather.state).simulations).toEqual({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 128, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 1, }, })

expect( selectGameplayVisibility(afterFirstGather.state).simulations, ).toEqual({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: true, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 128, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 1, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Actual worker generation before/at one batch produces fractional progress but only manual gather unlocks Simulations after Reality visit; tests route discovery, ready workers and lifetime manual credit as distinct stages.

declarations.title: does not unlock Simulations from automatic Influence
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(automaticInfluenceOnly).simulations).toEqual({ routeVisible: false, routeUnlocked: false, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 0, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 0, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Automatic influence counter alone cannot satisfy manual Simulations unlock; positive manual-gather scenario would pass even if both kinds incorrectly qualified.

declarations.title: keeps Simulations unlocked for an existing save with Simulation progress
assertions: expect(selectGameplayVisibility(existingSimulationSave).simulations).toEqual({ routeVisible: true, routeUnlocked: true, unlockProgress: { currentInfluence: 128, requiredInfluence: 128, fraction: 1, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Existing Simulation resource ownership preserves access despite otherwise first-run prerequisite fields; new-player progression tests cannot detect imported-save regression.

declarations.title: projects an exact next Universe Designation beyond the discrete ceiling
declarations.manualRationale: Universe designation above signed discrete ceiling projects exact bigint current and next values; bounded currency tests do not cover this intentionally uncapped identity.

declarations.title: %s Max previews the exact affordable effect headroom and becomes maxed after purchase
declarations.manualRationale: For each booster, remaining effect headroom bounds Max despite lifetime earned/spent totals over cap; checks preview/purchase cost parity, oversized rejection and final maxed state. Distinct booster IDs use different fields and Influence step size.

declarations.title: empty wallet has a zero Max quantity without claiming the booster is maxed
declarations.manualRationale: Empty-wallet preview must report insufficient-points rather than already-maxed even though Max quantity is zero; headroom-exhausted cases cannot detect misclassified reason.

declarations.title: Influence Max preserves the final single-purchase saturation with %s remaining
declarations.manualRationale: Each remainder one through four is a partial Influence step and must permit exactly one saturating purchase, match single versus Max and reject two; normal five-point headroom arithmetic misses rounding/saturation branches.

declarations.title: the developer override unlocks all progression routes without changing their resources
declarations.manualRationale: Developer visibility override must expose all progression routes without mutating resources and normal mode stays false; normal route unlock tests cannot establish this explicit override.

declarations.title: entry is invisible until saved and a failed abandonment preserves the active run
assertions: expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...revisionEnvelope(app), command: { kind: 'challenge.abandon' } })).toMatchObject({ transition: { accepted: false } })
expect(await reopened.dispatchPlayer({ ...revisionEnvelope(reopened), command: { kind: 'challenge.abandon' } })).toMatchObject({ transition: { accepted: true } })
declarations.manualRationale: Gated challenge entry stays invisible until commit; failed abandonment retains active run across reopen and later abandon grants no reward. Domain reset tests omit durable publication/failure ordering.

declarations.title: galvanization publishes only after currency and ownership are durably saved
assertions: expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...revisionEnvelope(app), command: { kind: 'skill.galvanize', skillId: 'startHereTree' } })).toMatchObject({ transition: { accepted: false } })
declarations.manualRationale: Failed and gated galvanization verify currency plus ownership publish only after commit and survive reopen together; skill transaction arithmetic alone cannot prove commit-first delivery.

declarations.title: saves %s preset priority before publishing it and preserves it on immediate reopen
assertions: expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...revisionEnvelope(app), command })).toMatchObject({ transition: { accepted: false } })
declarations.manualRationale: Active assignment and saved preset are two command routes, each tested against failed/gated commit and immediate reopen preserving priority. Regular checkpoint tests do not prove these edits themselves commit first.

declarations.title: completes at the ordinary boundary with Break unlocked, mode=%s
assertions: expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...revisionEnvelope(app), command: { kind: 'challenge.enter-blank-slate' } })).toMatchObject({ transition: { accepted: true } })
expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...revisionEnvelope(app), command: { kind: 'infinity.request-reset' } })).toMatchObject({ transition: { accepted: true } })
expect(complete.gameState.challenges).toMatchObject({ active: null, blankSlateCompleted: true, galvanizers: 1n, hasEarnedGalvanizer: true })
declarations.manualRationale: Manual, automatic and worker Stored Time completion paths must finish Blank Slate at ordinary threshold even with Break unlocked, grant one Galvanizer and survive reopen; shared expected reward does not make distinct execution lanes redundant.

declarations.title: an abrupt stop after an autosave recovers a day exactly once, including upgraded capacity
declarations.manualRationale: Abrupt-stop autosave followed by a day away credits exactly once, persists new baseline and credits a later minute; directly characterizes fallback timestamps and repeat-start suppression.

declarations.title: focus callbacks during active play do not replay an active checkpoint
declarations.manualRationale: Active-session focus callbacks after autosave must not count elapsed foreground as away time; cold restart uses a different admission path.

declarations.title: the actual departure timestamp wins over an older active checkpoint
declarations.manualRationale: Real departure recorded after autosave must override older active baseline and credit only thirty seconds, catching precedence errors absent when dateQuitString is null.

declarations.title: failed replay retains the baseline through another checkpoint and can retry
assertions: expect(await session.coordinator.handlePlatformPhase('active', undefined, { status: 'valid', utcMilliseconds: start + day - 1000, })).toMatchObject({ storedTimeCreditedSeconds: 86400 })
declarations.manualRationale: Failed away commit retains old baseline even through a later checkpoint, then retries full day despite supplied pending departure marker; successful replay cannot establish rollback/retry durability.

declarations.title: imports clear the sender fallback while retaining their bank
declarations.manualRationale: Imported save clears sender active timestamp while keeping its bank, so startup invents no elapsed years; legacy-null baseline tests do not traverse import preparation.

declarations.title: legacy/invalid baseline %s never creates invented away time
declarations.manualRationale: Both absent and malformed active-baseline inputs produce no-quit-timestamp and zero bank; these exercise missing versus invalid parser outcomes and protect legacy saves.

declarations.title: clock reversal grants zero and consumes the future baseline
declarations.manualRationale: Future baseline from clock reversal grants zero but durably consumes/reset baseline to now; null/invalid timestamps do not test a valid negative interval.

declarations.title: captures existing generated authorities without frontend defaults
declarations.manualRationale: Production event context must copy/freeze generated definitions and catalog assets rather than alias mutable authorities; input equality alone would not establish detachment and freeze.

declarations.title: captures retained host progress tuning in the production event context
declarations.manualRationale: Explicit host progress tuning of nine must override default four and be frozen; default context test never supplies retained host tuning.

declarations.title: invokes the authentic first-run seam only after repository discovery and checkpoints it
assertions: expect(application.start()).resolves.toMatchObject({ phase: 'ready', source: 'first-run', revision: { session: 1, state: 0, durable: 0, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Factory construction reads host ownership once but defers first-run save creation until repository discovery, then checkpoints and publishes exact revision/frozen entitlements. Direct startup resolver tests omit factory timing/ownership capture.

declarations.title: fails closed when the host entitlement authority is malformed
declarations.manualRationale: Malformed host permanentDoubleIp string must fail before first-run creation; valid host ownership composition cannot prove fail-closed type validation.

declarations.title: full-cap purchase, earn again, capped preview, checkpoint and restart preserve exact progress
assertions: expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...envelope(app), command: { kind: 'quantum.purchase-upgrade', upgradeId: 'CashBonus', quantity: 'max', } })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'transition', transition: { accepted: true, changed: true } })
expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...envelope(app), command: { kind: 'quantum.request-leap' } })) .toMatchObject({ kind: 'transition', transition: { accepted: true, changed: true } })

expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...envelope(app), command: { kind: 'quantum.purchase-upgrade', upgradeId: 'InfluenceSpeed', quantity: 2n, } })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'transition', transition: { accepted: false } })

expect(await app.dispatchPlayer({ ...envelope(app), command: { kind: 'quantum.purchase-upgrade', upgradeId, quantity, } })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'transition', transition: { accepted: true, changed: true } })

expect(snapshot(app).state.gameState.quantum).toMatchObject({ pointsEarned: DISCRETE_MAXIMUM + 100n, pointsSpent: DISCRETE_MAXIMUM + 11n, cashBonusLevels: DISCRETE_MAXIMUM, scienceBonusLevels: 10n, influenceSpeedBonus: DISCRETE_MAXIMUM, })
declarations.manualRationale: Integrated full-cap Cash purchase, earn-again leap, overlarge Influence rejection, partial saturation, Science purchase, checkpoint/restart and active advance protects the cumulative quantum ledger across application and persistence. Individual preview/unit cases cannot replace this multi-step state history.

declarations.title: retains dynamically unrefundable ownership without rewriting any preset
declarations.manualRationale: Dynamic unrefundable dependency ownership survives switching to empty target while all preset objects retain identity; static nonrefundable or ordinary purchase tests do not establish retained closure without layout rewriting.

declarations.title: keeps locked and merely unaffordable target Skills queued
declarations.manualRationale: Target includes locked and unaffordable skills with one point; switching must queue all without purchasing or mutating saved desired layout. Refund/conflict tests have different availability states.

declarations.title: applies dependency add/remove cascades to only the selected preset
declarations.manualRationale: Add/remove dependency cascade applies to selected slot three and active queue while four other slot object identities remain unchanged; direct dependency helpers lack selected-preset synchronization.

declarations.title: reapplies the selected desired queue after Infinity and a higher reset clears retained conflicts
declarations.manualRationale: A retained conflicting skill first blocks selection, then Infinity and Quantum reset clear conflict and reapply desired high-tier queue while preserving layout identity; standalone resets do not assert this preset conflict history.

declarations.title: preserves five distinct layouts through checkpoint, reload, export, and import
declarations.manualRationale: Mature schema08 imported runtime preserves five independent layouts and selected slot through both local checkpoint and portable import. Native integration matches asserted layout values but starts a first-run profile; retaining this migrated-source roundtrip avoids dropping the old-save compatibility witness merely because the final values match.

declarations.title: publishes progress but exposes the candidate only after persistence
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ committed: true, consumedSeconds: 2, remainingSeconds: 0, summary: { preset: 'balanced', simulationUpdates: 40, accuracyReduced: false, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Normal two-second worker replay commits once, debits bank to eight, emits running→idle and returns balanced forty-update summary. It does not itself gate publication timing, but asserts default completion/reporting values not covered by Speed Up summary.

declarations.title: returns committed first-disaster discoveries without publishing banner events
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ committed: true, summary: { firstDisasterOccurrences: [{ cause: 'Meteor', strangeMatterGranted: 1, resetCount: 1n, preResetEra: 'information', }], }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Worker first-disaster discoveries must flow into committed summary without appending live banner events; active-disaster engine test intentionally publishes banners instead.

declarations.title: reports the actual update count after repeated Speed Ups
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ committed: true, summary: { preset: 'balanced', simulationUpdates: 500, accuracyReduced: true, }, })
declarations.manualRationale: Two Speed Ups during a hundred-second job must report actual 500 updates and accuracyReduced while retaining original balanced preset; default replay summary has no speed changes.

declarations.title: persists unowned Quantum behavior through Stored Time and reload
assertions: expect(application.commitAwayReplacement( { sessionRevision: initial.revision.session, expectedStateRevision: initial.revision.state, }, candidate, )).resolves.toMatchObject({ committed: true })

expect(application.commitStoredTime( { sessionRevision: ready.revision.session, expectedStateRevision: ready.revision.state, }, 1, )).resolves.toMatchObject({ committed: true, consumedSeconds: 1, remainingSeconds: 0, })
declarations.manualRationale: With Break and Entanglement unowned, worker replay produces ordinary one-IP reset without Quantum earnings/unlock changes and persists that state; max-cap Quantum certification starts owned.

declarations.title: contains a throwing status subscriber without changing the committed result
assertions: expect(application.commitStoredTime({ sessionRevision: snapshot.revision.session, expectedStateRevision: snapshot.revision.state, }, 2)).resolves.toMatchObject({ committed: true, consumedSeconds: 2, })
declarations.manualRationale: Throwing job-status observer cannot prevent successful commit or idle cleanup; general snapshot subscriber isolation does not cover this separate status channel.

declarations.title: does not persist or charge a cancelled detached candidate
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ committed: false, consumedSeconds: 0, remainingSeconds: 2, code: 'CANONICAL-STORED-TIME-CANCELLED', })
declarations.manualRationale: Worker-reported cancelled terminal after progress must commit nothing and debit zero bank; main-thread cancellation cases deliberately receive completed rather than cancelled terminal.

declarations.title: discards completed work after %s cancellation without charging the bank
declarations.manualRationale: Each user/background/import/lifecycle cancellation reason must discard later completed worker result without debit and retain first reason despite another background request; separate codes are part of user-visible cancellation contract.

declarations.title: captures one immutable pre-job export and switches atomically to the committed result
declarations.manualRationale: Export while worker is gated returns detached pre-job bank and switches to current committed bank afterward while original capture stays immutable; ordinary save export lacks occupied-lane behavior.

declarations.title: rejects a concurrent request before replacing or cancelling the active job
assertions: expect(application.storedTimeJobStatus()).toMatchObject({ kind: 'cancelling', jobId: originalStatus.kind === 'idle' ? undefined : originalStatus.jobId, computedSeconds: 1, fraction: 0.5, })
declarations.manualRationale: Second simultaneous request rejects without replacing active status identity or invoking runner again, then original cancellation retains progress/job ID until idle; cancellation alone cannot prove admission exclusivity.

declarations.title: keeps the pre-job state when persistence rejects the candidate
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ committed: false, consumedSeconds: 0, remainingSeconds: 2, code: 'APP-COMMIT-FIRST-FAILED', })
declarations.manualRationale: Completed valid worker result followed by repository failure leaves pre-job bank and reports APP-COMMIT-FIRST-FAILED; worker invalid/cancelled paths never attempt persistence.

declarations.title: enters a non-cancellable committing phase before durable persistence
declarations.manualRationale: Gated durable write exposes non-cancellable committing phase; cancellation during this phase must not interrupt successful final debit and idle cleanup, unlike pre-commit cancellation.

declarations.title: rejects a partial worker completion before persistence
assertions: expect(application.commitStoredTime({ sessionRevision: snapshot.revision.session, expectedStateRevision: snapshot.revision.state, }, 2)).resolves.toMatchObject({ committed: false, consumedSeconds: 0, code: 'STORED-TIME-WORKER-CANDIDATE-INVALID', })
declarations.manualRationale: Tampered partial completion reports only one of requested two seconds: reject before any repository write or bank debit. Valid full completion and entitlement tampering use different validation predicates.

declarations.title: commits a final-update skill-driven bot cap and preserves it across reload
assertions: expect(result).toMatchObject({ committed: true, consumedSeconds: 0.1, remainingSeconds: 0, summary: { simulationUpdates: 2, remainingBankSeconds: 0, infinityCount: 0n, infinityPoints: 0n, }, })
expect(committed.state.gameState.infinity).toMatchObject({ points: pointsBefore, botCapTransitionPending: true, botCapRewardsGranted: false, inProgress: false, })
expect(durable.state.gameState.infinity).toMatchObject({ points: pointsBefore, botCapTransitionPending: true, botCapRewardsGranted: false, inProgress: false, })
declarations.manualRationale: Final skill-driven Overflow update must settle once, report zero Infinity gain, persist pending flag/bank zero across reopen and not reward on resumed active tick; synchronous replay test omits worker result validation and persistence.

declarations.title: rejects an unsettled bot-cap candidate before persistence
assertions: expect(application.commitStoredTime({ sessionRevision: snapshot.revision.session, expectedStateRevision: snapshot.revision.state, }, 2)).resolves.toMatchObject({ committed: false, consumedSeconds: 0, code: 'STORED-TIME-WORKER-CANDIDATE-INVALID', reason: 'The worker candidate contains an unsettled bot-cap checkpoint.', })
declarations.manualRationale: Worker returning MAX_VALUE bots without settled checkpoint must reject with specific unsettled-cap reason before persistence; numeric validity alone would accept finite bots.

declarations.title: rejects a worker mutation of session-owned carriers before persistence
assertions: expect(application.commitStoredTime({ sessionRevision: snapshot.revision.session, expectedStateRevision: snapshot.revision.state, }, 2)).resolves.toMatchObject({ committed: false, consumedSeconds: 0, code: 'STORED-TIME-WORKER-CANDIDATE-INVALID', })
declarations.manualRationale: Worker changing host-owned permanentDoubleIp must reject before persistence despite otherwise valid simulation; partial-duration and bot-cap tests do not establish session carrier ownership.

declarations.title: falls back to a 16-byte lowercase hexadecimal token

declarations.title: preserves the 12-byte legacy identifier fallback width

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: allows exactly one simultaneous acquisition
declarations.manualRationale: Two BrowserWriterLease instances concurrently acquire against shared storage, then blocked instance cannot enter callback. Lower-level database acquisition tests do not assert lease state or authoritative callback admission.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: supports explicit release and monotonically fenced handoff
declarations.manualRationale: Explicit release followed by blocked-owner retry must advance generation from one to two, covering deliberate handoff rather than expiry takeover.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: recovers an expired owner and rejects every stale mutation
declarations.manualRationale: Expired lease replaced by another owner must reject stale storage write and renewal, keep verified bytes and mark lease lost; no-expiry release does not cover clock-based invalidation.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: preserves the last verified save when quota aborts atomic promotion
assertions: expect( repository.commit( PreparedSave.fromDecoded({ saveVersion: 12, marker: 'candidate', }), ), ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'quota-exceeded', })
declarations.manualRationale: Repository commit through fenced IndexedDB adapter receives quota failure on replace and must retain exactly the last verified serialized primary; database transaction test below injects request failure at a different abstraction boundary.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: records persistent-storage denial and quota pressure without claiming durability
assertions: expect(status).toEqual({ persistenceSupported: true, persistenceRequested: true, persisted: false, usageBytes: 95, quotaBytes: 100, remainingBytes: 5, quotaPressure: true, })
declarations.manualRationale: Storage API denies persistent allocation with 95% quota usage: reports unsupported durability honestly and computes remaining capacity/pressure. Lease and repository tests do not inspect storage capability reporting.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: enforces a heartbeat no slower than half the lease and no longer than ten seconds
assertions: expect( () => new BrowserWriterLease({ database, ownerToken: 'invalid', leaseDurationMilliseconds: 1_000, heartbeatMilliseconds: 501, }), ).toThrow('no more than half')
expect( () => new BrowserWriterLease({ database, ownerToken: 'invalid', leaseDurationMilliseconds: 30_000, heartbeatMilliseconds: 10_001, }), ).toThrow('at most 10 seconds')
declarations.manualRationale: Construction rejects heartbeat both slower than half lease and above ten seconds, independent invalid configuration branches absent in operational lease tests.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: acquire racing release never republishes writable and releases the acquired fence once
declarations.manualRationale: Gated acquisition resolves after release: acquired fence must be released exactly once without publishing writable or acquired notice. Dispose race differs in terminal state and notice closure semantics.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: wakes a blocked lease when the owning context announces release
declarations.manualRationale: Release notice received by blocked lease updates its retry expiry immediately; ordinary acquisition/release tests have no notice-channel delivery to blocked observers.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: dispose racing acquire is immediately terminal and publishes nothing afterward
declarations.manualRationale: Disposal while acquire pending must synchronously cancel/fence, release late grant once, close notice channel and never emit later state/notice; normal release intentionally emits a release notice.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: heartbeat racing release cannot publish renewal after terminal release
declarations.manualRationale: An in-flight heartbeat resolves after release: prevent renewal publication and duplicate release while retaining acquired/released notice sequence. Acquire-race tests do not exercise renew completion.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: database takeover blocks operation entry before the callback runs
declarations.manualRationale: Forced database ownership takeover before operation invocation must prevent callback entry and set cancellation/lost; stale mutation tests already entered storage operations.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: in-flight authority exposes expiry cancellation and rejects a late result
declarations.manualRationale: Gated admitted operation crosses its expiry deadline, exposes cancellation through held signal and rejects late result. Entry-time takeover cannot detect authority expiring mid-operation.

ancestors: browser writer ownership and fenced persistence
declarations.title: database loss flips cancellation for an operation already in flight
declarations.manualRationale: Forced database takeover during admitted work plus assertWritable must flip the already-issued signal and reject late completion, unlike expiry-driven cancellation which changes the clock.

declarations.title: reuses the tab token only for a reload
declarations.manualRationale: Fresh navigation then reload must persist/reuse one session token and enable same-owner takeover only on reload; this establishes no-existing-token startup unlike inherited-token replacement.

declarations.title: replaces an inherited token on every non-reload navigation
declarations.manualRationale: An inherited token simulates duplicated tabs; replacement must precede that new tab reload, so simple empty-storage reload coverage cannot catch accidental cross-tab authority reuse.

declarations.title: retains the deployed schema-13 browser backup namespace for recovery
declarations.manualRationale: Exact deployed namespace strings preserve discovery of historical backups, retained imports and Stored Time sidecars. Native-root and actual current-save paths are different compatibility contracts.

declarations.title: serializes simultaneous production lease acquisition to exactly one writer
declarations.manualRationale: Real IndexedDbBrowserSaveDatabase over serialized IDB harness must issue one winning metadata write for concurrent acquisitions; memory BrowserSaveDatabase tests replace this production transaction implementation.

declarations.title: atomically replaces files and rejects a stale production fence
assertions: expect( database.mutateFiles( { kind: 'write', path: '/current', contents: 'stale' }, first.fence, 2_001, ), ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(WriterLeaseLostError)
declarations.manualRationale: Exercises production write/temporary replace/delete and then stale-generation write rejection, asserting destination and temporary state. Lease-only mocked persistence does not cover transaction file operations.

declarations.title: reconstructs a verified repository through a fresh production database instance
declarations.manualRationale: Fresh production database/repository wrapper must retain a migrated prepared save including an unknown marker; broad gameplay composition reconstruction does not assert compatibility fields outside canonical mapping.

declarations.title: aborts a quota-failed atomic replace and reconstructs the prior primary through a fresh wrapper
declarations.manualRationale: Injected IDB files-put quota failure must abort exactly one transaction and a fresh wrapper must see old primary; in-memory adapter quota injection cannot prove production IDB abort handling.

declarations.title: copies and retains exact recovery text through the production adapter and a fresh wrapper
assertions: expect( await reconstructedStorage.discoverLegacyCandidates(), ).toEqual([ { id: 'retained-id', sourcePath: 'browser-import/retained-id', text: 'IDB1:exact-retained-candidate', provenance: { kind: 'browser-retained-import' }, }, ])
declarations.manualRationale: Production adapter copy plus retainLegacyCandidate must preserve exact recovery bytes, candidate path and browser-retained provenance after wrapper recreation; gameplay checkpoint reconstruction lacks retained-import metadata.

declarations.title: rejects corrupt generation $generation before any lease write
declarations.manualRationale: Each corrupt generation (negative, fractional, maximum-safe unable to increment) must fail before any metadata put and preserve stored record. These represent distinct validation/overflow classes, not arbitrary repeated numeric samples.

declarations.title: reopens after version change and unexpected close, retries blocked opens, and closes late success
declarations.manualRationale: Exercises versionchange, unexpected close, blocked open retry and late successful connection closure using the production connection cache; ordinary open/reconstruction tests do not trigger these lifecycle callbacks.

declarations.title: allows an explicit same-owner reload takeover and fences the previous document
assertions: expect(reloaded).toMatchObject({ acquired: true, fence: { ownerToken: 'same-tab', generation: 2, expiresAtUtcMilliseconds: 16_100, }, })
expect( database.mutateFiles( { kind: 'write', path: '/current', contents: 'stale' }, first.fence, 1_100, ), ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(WriterLeaseLostError)
declarations.manualRationale: Explicit same-owner unexpired reload takeover increments generation and fences prior document; expired takeover and different-owner recovery use distinct permission gates.

declarations.title: allows a deliberate recovery takeover to fence a different live owner

declarations.title: does not duplicate a delayed current-state reconciliation that matches the conservative phase
declarations.manualRationale: Delayed background reconciliation must not publish a duplicate initial background notification; the stale-event case also has a newer event, so its suppression has a different cause.

declarations.title: keeps the subscribed lifecycle stream when the current-state query fails
declarations.manualRationale: Rejected initial query must leave the already-registered event stream usable; successful initial query ordering does not cover failure cleanup behavior.

declarations.title: selects native before constructing browser persistence
declarations.manualRationale: Actual host selector receives native bridge while browser factory throws; asserts browser persistence never opens and PWA is disabled, proving runtime selection rather than static import placement.

declarations.title: uses the mobile checkpoint policy for Android and iOS hosts
declarations.manualRationale: Both Android and iOS composition must receive MOBILE_LIFECYCLE_POLICY rather than desktop WEB policy; desktop injection test intentionally uses electron.

declarations.title: normalizes a partial native catalog without inventing availability
